name: Roomvana
tagline: Upload a photo of a room and get AI-generated redesigns in different styles.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The whole product is one API call wrapped in a nice upload form: photo in, depth or edge map out, image model back in, pretty render out. An agent can build that loop in an afternoon, and the open source ancestor of this entire app genre has existed for years. The catch is that the quality you actually want comes from a tuned pipeline, good prompts per style, and a hosted image model you pay per generation for, so you trade a subscription for a metered API bill. Running it fully local means a GPU and a ControlNet setup, which is no longer one sitting. Also, nothing you build will have the credit-free, instant, phone-friendly feel of the paid thing, and for a one-off kitchen reno you may just not care.
coreLoopDIY: Upload a room photo, pick a style preset, run it through a depth-conditioned image model, and get a before/after comparison you can download.
requirements: An image model API key (Replicate, Fal, or similar) or a local GPU with ControlNet
Pay-per-generation budget, since renders are not free
whatYouLose: Style presets that someone actually tuned, instead of your first-draft prompt strings
Mobile-friendly capture flow and fast queueing on someone else's GPUs
Room detection, masking, and furniture-swap features if the paid tool has them
Predictable flat pricing instead of a metered API bill that spikes when you get excited
Any shareable gallery, project history, or client-facing presentation layer
moatNotes: The moat here is prompt and pipeline tuning plus a smooth upload-to-render flow, not data. Nobody is locked in.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the gap between a raw depth-ControlNet render and something that looks like a real room is all tuning, and tuning is boring. People pay to skip the prompt archaeology, get twenty usable variations in two minutes on their phone, and not think about GPU queues or API credits. If you are redecorating one apartment once, the subscription is cheaper than your weekend.
notes: This is the single most cloned AI app shape in existence, which tells you something about how hard the core is.
prompt:
Build a local web app called "Roomshop" that redesigns photos of rooms with AI.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3 for render history, local filesystem for images. No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no external analytics. Single user, runs on localhost.

Flow:
1. Home page: drag and drop or file-pick a room photo. Show a preview. Max 10MB, jpg/png/webp only.
2. Pick a room type from a dropdown: living room, bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, home office, dining room.
3. Pick a style from preset cards: Scandinavian, Mid-Century Modern, Industrial Loft, Japandi, Maximalist, Coastal, Brutalist. Each preset is a hand-written prompt fragment stored in a single styles.ts file with full prompt text, negative prompt, and a strength value. Make these editable in code and document them.
4. Optional free-text "extra instructions" field appended to the prompt.
5. Submit calls POST /api/render which: saves the upload to ./data/uploads, calls Replicate with a depth-conditioned ControlNet SDXL model (read REPLICATE_API_TOKEN from .env.local, model slug in an env var so it can be swapped), requests 4 variations, saves results to ./data/renders, writes a row to SQLite with source path, result paths, room type, style, full prompt, and timestamp.
6. Results page: 2x2 grid of renders, click one to open a before/after slider against the original, download button per image.
7. /history page: reverse-chronological list of past jobs with thumbnails, click to reopen results, delete button that removes files and the row.

In scope: the render loop, presets, history, before/after slider, download.
Out of scope: user accounts, payments, sharing links, furniture product matching, object masking, mobile app, image upscaling.

Requirements: show the actual API cost estimate per render in the UI, hard-fail with a readable error if REPLICATE_API_TOKEN is missing, queue one job at a time and show a real progress state rather than a fake spinner. Write a README with setup, env vars, and a short note on how to swap in a local ComfyUI endpoint instead of Replicate. Commit a .env.example, never a real key.
